sentences.text: Hudsonelpidia was a tiny ichthyosaur, a marine reptile, found in British Columbia. The only known example is a nearly complete skeleton measuring under two meters long.
This single specimen preserves the skull along with the rest of the body.
Chris McGowan created the genus name in 1995, using Hudsonelpidia brevirostris as the type species.
The bones were found on the northern shore of the Peace Reach branch of Williston Lake.
Studies of its evolutionary relationships show it occupies a consistent spot in many analyses.
Researchers placed the animal in the family Hudsonelpidiidae and the unranked group Parvipelvia.
These fossils date to the middle Norian stage of the Late Triassic, roughly 210 million years ago.
Scientists estimate the animal lived between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
